text:
incident-bot: Pager ALERT: high p99 latency detected for /v1/chat/completions (route: chat.user, group: chat-completions). p99=3.2s, p95=850ms. Triggered at 2026-03-17T14:12:09Z. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/latency/chat-completions?panel=4 :pager:

eric: oncall here, looking. any customer-visible errors or 5xxs?

maria: seen some user complaints in #support — roughly 15% error rate for a subset of requests (longer context). Not full outage, but latency spikes causing timeouts in some frontends.

jonathan: seeing concurrent spike from a single downstream: AcmeApp prod region eu-west-1, a lot of 4k token prompts. KV cache miss rate jumped.

kevin_sre: attaching quick trace sample: ```trace_id: a1b2c3 -> model=mistral-7b v2 -> token_seq=4096 -> decode_time=2.8s``` suspect model decode path + long seqs.

liz: TL;DR: p99 alert is noisy because it lumps all models and routes. propose: temporarily squelch the global p99 alert and create per-model per-route p99 alerts + a prefix-length filter.

eric: agree. mitigation options: 1) temporary alert mute for chat-completions p99 (15m), 2) enable automatic fallback to smaller variant (mistral-7b -> mistral-7b-q4) for routes exceeding seq len threshold, 3) add dashboard panel for per-model p99 by route. Which do we want UAT first?

sam_product: if AcmeApp is customer-facing, sales should be notified. Sam, can you reach out to AMs? :phone:

sam_product: pinged AMs, they're on call and will notify Acme success team.

kevin_sre: I'll take the alert config change. Proposed alert rule snippet to split by model and route:

```yaml
alert: HighP99PerModelRoute
expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{endpoint="/v1/chat/completions"}[5m])) by (le, route, model)) > 1.5
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "p99 > 1.5s for {{ $labels.model }} / {{ $labels.route }}"
```

kevin_sre: implementing now, then will mute old global alert for 15m. Will also add a tag to the incident for follow-up.

maria: customer impact note: AcmeApp accounts for ~42% of requests for that route in eu-west-1. If we fallback to q4 quantized variant, small accuracy risk but big latency improvement. Recommend canary to 5% then ramp if ok.

eric: do it. Kevin, enable canary routing policy to shift 5% of Acme traffic to mistral-7b-q4 for 10 minutes, monitor p50/p95/p99. If p99 drops below 1.0s, ramp to 50%.

kevin_sre: done: canary started at 2026-03-17T14:20:40Z. Initial metrics: p99 for the canary 0.9s, error rate stable. Old global alert temporarily muted for 15m.

liz: follow-ups: ticket INF-4321 to implement permanent per-model-per-route alerts + add prefix-length dimension to alerting. Also create dashboard tile: "p99 by model x route x prefix_len_bucket". Assign to eng-observability.

jonathan: note for runbook: add step to check top callers and token length distribution before muting global alerts. saves noise later.

sam_product: flagged customer comms follow-up in the ticket. AMs will send a note if we ramp to broader fallback.

eric: closing the pager. Will update postmortem template with threshold rationale and the new alert names. Thanks all :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident annotated: INF-2026-03-17-07. Actions: global p99 muted (15m), per-model-route alert created, canary fallback applied to AcmeApp (5%). See runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/latency-unbundle
